task.title: Brake Pad Replacement Procedure
task.shortdesc: Step-by-step instructions for removing, inspecting, and installing front disc brake pads.

prereq.p: Park the vehicle on a level surface and secure the center stand.
prereq.note: Brake fluid damages painted surfaces. Wipe spills immediately with a clean, dry cloth.
prereq.p: Required Tools: 12 mm socket wrench, 8 mm hex key, vernier caliper, torque wrench.

step.cmd: Loosen the guide pin (Item 1) and lock pin (Item 2) by two turns using an 8 mm hex key.
step.info: Do not remove the pins completely at this stage.

step.cmd: Remove the caliper mounting bolts securing the caliper body (Item 10) to the fork bracket.
Slide the caliper body (Item 10) backward away from the brake rotor.
step.stepresult: The caliper is now free from the wheel assembly.

step.cmd: Unscrew and remove guide pin (Item 1) and lock pin (Item 2).
Remove the inner pad with wear indicator (Item 11) and the outer pad (Item 12).
Measure the friction lining thickness of both pads using a vernier caliper.
step.stepresult: If the lining thickness is less than 1.5 mm, replace both pads as a complete set.

step.cmd: Clean the caliper bracket, pad clips, and guide pins with approved brake cleaner.
Install the new inner pad (Item 11) and outer pad (Item 12) into the caliper support (Item 4).
Tighten the guide pin (Item 1) to 27 Nm and lock pin (Item 2) to 22 Nm using a torque wrench.

postreq.p: Pump the brake lever several times to seat the pads against the rotor before operating the vehicle.
